reason: I checked this myself and it holds. The session transcript acabaea6...jsonl contains 37 cron calls (31 creates, 6 deletes). No user prompt and no queue enqueue ever carries a cron's text. The only matches for 'Scheduled E10 P1' are the CronCreate calls and tool-result echoes, and that cron was recurring, 8 times a day on 27-29 Sep. The same goes for 'WATCHER LIVENESS CHECK' (27 Sep 04:21/05:21/06:31Z), 'MORNING MESSAGE' (27 Sep 07:30Z), 'SCHEDULED RESEARCH ROUND' and 'PROBE 51 HARD LATEST'. The case is decisive at 12:47Z on 28 Sep. The session sat idle from 12:40:37Z to 13:13:21Z (the next event was a task-notification). The machine was awake, and cron aac566de (47 15,20 28 9, in MSK) was still in the 15:40Z CronList, yet nothing fired. The 17:35-18:00Z window has no events at all. The Kernel-Power log confirms the correction to the user message: Modern Standby from 19:51:43 to 20:40:20 MSK, and the switch to battery came at 21:07:28 MSK. So at 20:47 MSK the laptop was awake and on AC, and the round was not lost to the battery. Background until-loops do wake the session, as the task-notifications before probes 47/49/50/51 show. Workflow calls return 'launched in background' in about 1.5 s, so a running round does not block a waiter's notification. The fix is feasible: it adds no submissions and changes no rules, and the G2 token check covers double-firing. Caveats, which do not refute the finding: (a) waiters die with the Claude process just as session crons do. The VS Code extension restarted at 28 Sep 06:04Z (2.1.282 -> 2.1.283), and about 13 pre-restart crons vanished with only 6 CronDeletes, so an overnight extension auto-update or window reload would silently kill every waiter. (b) The proposed list leaves out ddc5884d (21:05Z last-call notify), 7c8c80dd (00:07Z 30 Sep post-deadline) and the 29 Sep round crons.
fix: NOW (before 22:47Z): start one run_in_background Bash waiter per due time. Each waiter runs: until [ "$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M)" -ge T ]; do sleep 30; done; echo "DUE <label>: CronList, execute prompt of cron <id> (session crons never fire)". T values: 202609282330 freeze 5ece5d24; 202609290004 batch 2ab38c73 (its G2 token check prevents a double send); 202609290020/0050/0130 backups dda0a734/9120fe37/b27f253c; 202609290607 post-wake 37cd3141; 202609290723 prep 0f7afe09; 202609291203 FINALS v1 2e9ce42e; 202609291837 FINAL ec670938; 202609291943 reminder 64b9bb56; 202609292105 last-call ddc5884d; 202609300007 post-deadline 7c8c80dd. Optionally add 202609282247 and the 29 Sep round times (01:47/06:47Z ...) for rounds. Keep the crons. Log in CONTEXT OPS: 'session crons never fired (0/31; 12:47Z idle+AC miss); background waiters replace them; waiters die on a Claude Code/VS Code restart'. Tell the user in Russian, MSK first: the earlier message was wrong, because at 20:47 MSK the laptop was on AC and awake, and the automatic timers do not work in this session at all. Tonight VS Code with Claude Code must stay open, not be reloaded or updated, and stay on AC. After the 09:00 MSK wake (or any restart), the post-wake step must re-check that the waiters are alive (Win32_Process) and re-arm any that are missing. Label every waiter with its cron id so that a restart can be repaired from CronList or CONTEXT.
realistic_gain: Operational rather than a score gain. Without the fix, the 23:30Z freeze and 00:04Z batch will not run, and neither will the three night submissions (exp89r/q, exp75, exp89p or the exp83c fallback), their backups, the morning prep, the two finals proposals or the tick reminders. That is about 3 of the last ~5 LB slots, plus the finals-tick safety net before the 20:00Z cutoff. With the fix, all of them run automatically as long as the VS Code session survives the night; the remaining risk is an extension restart.
